correctness.rationale: For a full-dimensional simple convex 3-polytope the normal cones of vertices give 2F-4 nondegenerate spherical triangles of total area 4π; E=3F-6. Complementary normal and interior angles make an obtuse edge precisely a short fan side. A triangle with all sides at least π/2 has the same lower bound on its angles by the spherical cosine law and hence area at least π/2. For F>=7 there are at least ten triangles, so eight good ones plus the others cannot fit. At most 2m triangles meet a short side, yielding 2F-4-2m<=7 and m>=F-5 by integrality. The finite-facet witness checks: the horizontal normals of the base tetrahedron positively surround zero and the three side planes meet above its nondegenerate base. The recurrence follows from (X-R)(X²+2X/R+1); its positive coefficients uniquely expose the last triple intersection. A support level between the signed value at the apex and the maximum signed value at the other vertices truncates only that vertex. Successive new facets meet precisely their three predecessors; the initial bottom adjacencies remain. At side gaps 1 and 2 the negative cosine dominates corrections bounded by R^-3 and R^-4; gap 3 is positive and the bottom products are negative. Hence exactly F-4 edges are obtuse. The unit-normal estimate gives the strict angle ceiling once arcsin(4/R)<δ. The two proportions squeeze to 1/3, without settling either of the two possible finite counts for F>=7. The bundled CHECKER.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected but not executed; the finite halfspace tests are supplementary.

evidence: Li–Wang–Yu construct examples with arbitrarily many faces under a near-right upper angle bound. The earlier pinching record requires a positive lower angle bound α>2δ and gives a facet upper bound independent of a count of obtuse edges.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Existence in a family and restrictions under two-sided pinching do not imply a one-sided universal lower count for all simple polytopes, including those with very acute edges.

evidence: Li–Wang–Yu give the side normals, gap-at-most-three incidence, and adjacent normal-product bound. The positive products at gap three yield F-4 without a new construction. Coxeter's theorem rules out the all-nonobtuse case except for classified polytopes.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior upper witness and zero-obtuse classification do not credit the lower bound with linear coefficient one. The quantitative counting of good triangles and the incidence bound for bad triangles supply the missing implication giving the limit.

evidence: A strictly obtuse interior edge is a side of length <π/2 in the spherical normal fan. The pinching record also uses the normal-fan area but applies two-sided side bounds uniformly, not a count of short sides. Coxeter handles the no-short-side case.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equivalent short-side count in spherical normal triangulations is not supplied by classification when the count is zero or by a bound under uniform pinching.
searches: Coxeter, Discrete Groups Generated by Reflections, Theorem 2

evidence: The graph-diameter record uses the very same apex-truncation realization and exact facet counts, but evaluates graph diameter. The two-sided record evaluates a facet bound. The witness count itself is obtainable from the prior normal and adjacency data.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Exact facet parameters and use of the same example cover the realization, not the infimum across all simple polytopes. There is no finite-table inference to the new lower count.

originality.rationale: Pass for the universal lower count and the resulting asymptotically exact density. Credit both the truncation family and the essentially immediate F-4 sign count from its published normals and adjacencies to the prior construction; they are not independent novelty claims. No equivalent universal count was established in the inspected sources.
residual_risks: An unexamined spherical triangulation or dihedral counting result might contain an equivalent bound. Priority is provisional and does not follow from same-day timestamps.
The established witness is prior; credit the new content only for the obstruction and resulting asymptotic law.

value.rationale: A known family already shows that the maximum dihedral angle may be arbitrarily close to right with arbitrarily many facets. Counting how many of those edges must cross the right-angle threshold is a distinct natural extremal question. The universal bound gives density one third up to an additive-one gap in absolute edge count uniformly in the angle cap, rather than merely detecting one obtuse edge.
